input.command: git status && git branch -vv && git log -5 --oneline && git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD && git rev-parse --abbrev-ref @{upstream} 2>/dev/null; ls -la /workspace

git log --oneline --all | head -30; echo '---'; git remote -v; echo '---'; git branch -a; echo '---'; git merge-base HEAD origin/main 2>/dev/null; git merge-base HEAD origin/master 2>/dev/null; git show --stat HEAD
git rev-parse HEAD^ 2>/dev/null; git log --format='%P %s' -1 HEAD; git cat-file -p HEAD | head -8

mkdir -p /opt/cursor/artifacts && node smoke.ts > /opt/cursor/artifacts/smoke.log 2>&1 && node scratch/check.ts > /opt/cursor/artifacts/scratch-check.log 2>&1 && cat /opt/cursor/artifacts/smoke.log /opt/cursor/artifacts/scratch-check.log

cat > /opt/cursor/artifacts/code-tour-author-handoff.md << 'EOF'
<decision>
Nightly late fee is 2% of the unpaid remainder, halved when the invoice is overdue by less than seven 24-hour days, because this automates accounting’s existing first-week practice rather than raising the fee to a flat 2% without an explicit product change. Alternatives set aside: 2% of the original total, calendar-date due (ignore time of day), and dropping the half-fee as legacy.
</decision>
<risk>
Reviewers should confirm that “until now” was meant to keep the half-fee, not retire it, and that the fee is on remaining balance rather than `amountCents`. Exact due-timestamp vs next-calendar-day overdue can shift a nightly run by a few hours.
</risk>
<verified>
Ran `node smoke.ts` (exports `lateFeeCents`, neutral example returned 0) and `node scratch/check.ts` covering not-due, first-week half fee, 7+ day full fee, partial payment, fully paid, and rounding.
</verified>
EOF
ls -la /opt/cursor/artifacts/
git add impl.ts artifacts && git status && git diff --cached --stat && git log -3 --format='%an %ae' && git commit -m "Implement ticket" && git status && git push -u origin HEAD
